newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore products ease with crude, naphtha holds.
newsitem.headline: Singapore products ease with crude, naphtha holds.

text.p: Singapore oil products closed weaker on Tuesday on lower crude prices following of the shipment of Iraqi crude with the exception of bullish naphtha, traders said.

Naphtha prices held steady on good demand and firmer prices in North Asia. One Thai petrochemical plant was also heard seeking a second-half cargo. Singapore swaps were largely unchanged with January offered at $25.05 per barrel from a $25.15 bid on Monday. Naphtha's strength caused some concern and confusion in the gasoline market, with some spot assesments for naphtha now unusually higher than gasoline.
But some sellers still preferred to sell 95-octane gasoline on a naphtha related basis - at a premium of $1.25 to $3.00 per barrel - rather than at the low gasoline spot quotes.
Traders said the middle-distillate and fuel oil markets were dragged down by news of the sale of Iraqi crude oil which set crude prices down by about $1.00 a barrel since last Friday.

Physical gas oil was offered at $33.25 a barrel free-on-board Singapore, $1.20 below Friday's traded record level, but no buying interest emerged. January gas oil swaps also fell with trade at $31.77 a barrel, down from Friday's peak of $33.07.

But the gas oil market's slide has been dampened by large purchases by China, traders said. Earlier this week, China bought a prompt cargo from Thailand at $264 per tonne, cost-and-freight to south China and another 50,000-tonnes at a $1.30 premium to Singapore spot quotes c-and-f.
Jet fuel also edged down with a major offering to a low of $34.00 a barrel, fob Singapore, for a 165,000-barrel cargo loading in late December.
